sla_onsite.text: onID="2.0.2">CRITERION.EXCLUSION.CONVICTIONS.PARTICIPATION_IN_CRIMINAL_ORGANISATION</cbc:CriterionTypeCode> <cbc:Name>Osalemine kuritegelikus organisatsioonis</cbc:Name> <cbc:Description languageID="ET">Kas ettevõtja ise või tema haldus-, juht- või järelevalveorgani liige või isik, kellel on volitused seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on lõpliku süüdimõistva kohtuotsusega süüdi mõistetud kuritegelikus organisatsioonis osalemise eest kõige rohkem viimase viie aasta jooksul või kehtib süüdimõistvas kohtuotsuses sätestatud kõrvalejäämise kohustus endiselt?</cbc:Description> <cac:Legislation> <cbc:ID schemeID="CriteriaTaxonomy" schemeAgencyID="EU-COM-GROW" schemeVersionID="2.0.2">c753a2c5-59e6-4970-b6eb-27224e96bf76</cbc:ID> <cbc:Title languageID="ET">RHS § 95 lg 1 p 1 "keda või kelle haldus-, juhtimis- või järelevalveorgani liiget, prokuristi või muud isikut, kellel on volitus seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on karistatud kuritegelikus ühenduses osalemise eest". Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural pr

public health through development of data and knowledge that are translatable, predictive, and timely. The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based m

e approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based microphysiological systems and test methods that better model human health (in this case, the initial work will focus on liver). 3) Scope: The Contractor shall provide a Fluigent Microencapsulation Platform, in accordance with the obtained vendor quotation. The system shall include the require

formation of three-dimensional (3D) microtissues and organoids. The Contractor shall also provide installation and training for the Fluigent system at the NIEHS facility. Vendor representatives shall perform system setup and provide training to facilitate rapid onboarding and use of the technology. The system will operate independently of NIEHS information technology (IT) systems and will not require NIEHS IT support. The computer and software components are expected to be delivered by the end of September 2026. Full system installation and training are expected to be completed in Fall 2026, subject to vendor engineer scheduling availability.
